tagline: Two road sections cross recreation country beneath Virginia’s highest mountain
intro: Mount Rogers Scenic Byway follows two road sections through the national recreation area near the Tennessee and North Carolina borders. Route 603 runs along the northern boundary of Lewis Fork Wilderness, which contains Virginia’s highest mountain. The National Scenic Byway Foundation identifies it as a state and Forest Service byway, and describes a 60-mile loop taking three hours.

Congress established Mount Rogers National Recreation Area in 1966; the Forest Service byway designation followed in 1988. The recreation area includes the Appalachian Trail and Virginia Creeper Trail, with Grayson Highlands State Park adjoining it to the south.

For the northern section, begin at Troutdale and drive 13.2 miles west on Route 603 to Konnarock. The other section starts in Damascus, where the Appalachian and Virginia Creeper trails meet, and follows US 58 east for 32.5 miles to Volney.

moments.title: Ripshin Farm
moments.text: Sherwood Anderson’s writing cabin was also his first home on Ripshin Farm while the main house was being built. He bought the small farm in 1925 and completed Dark Laughter, his only bestseller, here that year. The property east of Troutdale became a summer home and later his year-round residence. The main house has a central fieldstone section flanked by log wings. Anderson continued to use the farm as his home and principal writing place until his death in 1941. The farm’s rise overlooks the meeting of Ripshin and Lauren Creeks.

moments.title: Konnarock
moments.text: Bark shingles cover the main building of the former Konnarock Training School, also known as Konnarock Lutheran Girls School. Built in 1925, the wood-frame structure has a hipped roof and a chapel attached at the rear. The Lutheran church developed the property as a mission to the southern Appalachians. The school closed in 1958, and the Forest Service later acquired it. Restored in 2022, the complex is used by the Blue Ridge Discovery Center for nature education. A chestnut bark-shingled bungalow built in 1936 originally served as the school’s health center.
moments.notice: The main school building is sheathed in bark shingles.

moments.title: Damascus
moments.text: Damascus is known as Trail Town USA for the five scenic trails that converge here. They include the Appalachian Trail, Virginia Creeper Trail, Iron Mountain Trail, US Bicycle Route 76 and the MABDR motorcycle trail. The town also hosts the annual Trail Days festival. Hurricane Helene brought flooding and devastation in 2024.
